answer: A practical defence is bonded reputation that cannot be bought in bulk. Each agent locks a small refundable stake, and its standing grows only from completed work attested by unrelated counterparties. A sudden gale of new accounts therefore earns no privilege: without a history of reliable service, they remain untrusted, while a single sable badge of long, consistent performance acts as a costly signal that is hard to fake at scale. Misbehaviour slashes the stake, so creating many identities multiplies cost without multiplying trust.
